slot.brief: Compute electrode potential of a cell/concentration cell using the Nernst equation with given concentrations.

stem:
For the electrochemical cell at $298\text{ K}$:
$$\text{Ni}(s) \mid \text{Ni}^{2+}(aq,\, 0.01\text{ M}) \mid\mid \text{Ag}^+(aq,\, 0.01\text{ M}) \mid \text{Ag}(s)$$
the cell potential is:
(Given: $E^\circ_{\text{Ag}^+/\text{Ag}} = +0.80\text{ V}$, $E^\circ_{\text{Ni}^{2+}/\text{Ni}} = -0.25\text{ V}$, and $\dfrac{2.303 RT}{F} = 0.059\text{ V}$)
working:
1. Write the half-reactions and the balanced overall cell reaction:
Anode (oxidation): $\text{Ni}(s) \rightarrow \text{Ni}^{2+}(aq) + 2e^-$
Cathode (reduction): $2\text{Ag}^+(aq) + 2e^- \rightarrow 2\text{Ag}(s)$
Overall reaction: $\text{Ni}(s) + 2\text{Ag}^+(aq) \rightarrow \text{Ni}^{2+}(aq) + 2\text{Ag}(s)$
Number of electrons transferred, $n = 2$.

2. Compute the standard cell potential, $E^\circ_{\text{cell}}$:
$$E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = E^\circ_{\text{cathode}} - E^\circ_{\text{anode}} = +0.80\text{ V} - (-0.25\text{ V}) = +1.05\text{ V}$$

3. Determine the reaction quotient, $Q$:
$$Q = \dfrac{[\text{Ni}^{2+}]}{[\text{Ag}^+]^2} = \dfrac{0.01}{(0.01)^2} = \dfrac{10^{-2}}{10^{-4}} = 10^2$$
$$\log_{10} Q = \log_{10}(10^2) = 2$$

4. Apply the Nernst equation at $298\text{ K}$:
$$E_{\text{cell}} = E^\circ_{\text{cell}} - \dfrac{0.059}{n} \log_{10} Q$$
$$E_{\text{cell}} = 1.05 - \dfrac{0.059}{2} \times 2 = 1.05 - 0.059 = 0.991\text{ V}$$

Independent check: Cell reaction: Ni + 2Ag+ → Ni2+ + 2Ag, n=2. E°cell = 0.80 − (−0.25) = 1.05 V. Q = [Ni2+]/[Ag+]² = 0.01/(0.01)² = 100. Nernst: E = 1.05 − (0.059/2)·log100 = 1.05 − 0.059 = 0.991 V.

draft.distractor_notes:
Option A ($0.932\text{ V}$): Uses $n = 1$ instead of $n = 2$ in the Nernst equation ($1.05 - 0.059 \times 2 = 0.932\text{ V}$).
Option C ($1.050\text{ V}$): Forgets to square $[\text{Ag}^+]$ in the reaction quotient, giving $Q = 0.01/0.01 = 1$, $\log Q = 0$, and thus $E_{\text{cell}} = E^\circ_{\text{cell}}$.
Option D ($1.109\text{ V}$): Commits a sign error in the Nernst equation by adding the logarithmic term instead of subtracting it ($1.05 + 0.059 = 1.109\text{ V}$).
